entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.3">Lev 20:3</reference> <div eID="gen1428" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1429" type="x-p"/> By this punishment the nation only carried out the will of Jehovah; for He would cut off such a man (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.17.10">Lev 17:10</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.18.21">Lev 18:21</reference>) for having defiled the sanctuary of Jehovah and desecrated the name of Jehovah, not because he had brought the sacrifice to Moloch into the sanctuary of Jehovah, as <hi type="italic">Movers</hi> supposes, but in the same sense in which all the sins of Israel defiled the sanctuary in their midst (<reference osisRef="Lev.15.31">Lev 15:31</reference>; <reference osisRef="Lev.16.16">Lev 16:16</reference>).

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.9-Lev.20.18">Lev 20:9-18</reference> <div eID="gen1432" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1433" type="x-p"/> Whoever cursed father or mother was to be punished with death (<reference osisRef="Lev.19.3">Lev 19:3</reference>); “<hi type="italic">His blood would be upon him</hi>.” The cursing of parents was a capital crime (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.17.4">Lev 17:4</reference>, and for the plural דּמיו <reference osisRef="Exod.22.1">Exo 22:1</reference> and <reference osisRef="Gen.4.10">Gen 4:10</reference>), which was to return upon the doer of it, according to Gen 9:6. The same punishment was to be inflicted upon adultery (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.10">Lev 20:10</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.20">Lev 18:20</reference>), carnal intercourse with a father’s wife (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.11">Lev 20:11</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.7-Lev.18.8">Lev 18:7-8</reference>) or with a daughter-in-law (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.12">Lev 20:12</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.17">Lev 18:17</reference>), sodomy (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.13">Lev 20:13</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.22">Lev 18:22</reference>), sexual intercourse with a mother and her daughter, in which case the punishment was to be heightened by the burning of the criminals when put to death (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.14">Lev 20:14</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.17">Lev 18:17</reference>), lying with a beast (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.15">Lev 20:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.16">Lev 20:16</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.23">Lev 18:23</reference>), sexual intercourse with a half-sister (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.17">Lev 20:17</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.9">Lev 18:9</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.18.11">Lev 18:11</reference>), and lying with a menstruous woman (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.18">Lev 20:18</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.19">Lev 18:19</reference>). The punishment of death, which was to be inflicted in all these cases upon both the criminals, and also upon the beast that had been abused (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.15">Lev 20:15</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.16">Lev 20:16</reference>), was to be by stoning, according to <reference osisRef="Lev.20.2">Lev 20:2</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.27">Lev 20:27</reference>, and Deu 22:21.; and by the burning (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.14">Lev 20:14</reference>) we are not to understand death by fire, or burning alive, but, as we may clearly see from <reference osisRef="Josh.7.15">Jos 7:15</reference> and <reference osisRef="Josh.7.25">Jos 7:25</reference>, burning the corpse after death. This was also the case in <reference osisRef="Lev.21.9">Lev 21:9</reference> and Gen 38:24.
entries.content_plain:
Lev 20:9-18 
 
 Whoever cursed father or mother was to be punished with death (Lev 19:3); “His blood would be upon him.” The cursing of parents was a capital crime (see at Lev 17:4, and for the plural דּמיו Exo 22:1 and Gen 4:10), which was to return upon the doer of it, according to Gen 9:6. The same punishment was to be inflicted upon adultery (Lev 20:10, cf. Lev 18:20), carnal intercourse with a father’s wife (Lev 20:11, cf. Lev 18:7-8) or with a daughter-in-law (Lev 20:12, cf. Lev 18:17), sodomy (Lev 20:13, cf. Lev 18:22), sexual intercourse with a mother and her daughter, in which case the punishment was to be heightened by the burning of the criminals when put to death (Lev 20:14, cf. Lev 18:17), lying with a beast (Lev 20:15, Lev 20:16, cf. Lev 18:23), sexual intercourse with a half-sister (Lev 20:17, cf. Lev 18:9 and Lev 18:11), and lying with a menstruous woman (Lev 20:18, cf. Lev 18:19). The punishment of death, which was to be inflicted in all these cases upon both the criminals, and also upon the beast that had been abused (Lev 20:15, Lev 20:16), was to be by stoning, according to Lev 20:2, Lev 20:27, and Deu 22:21.; and by the burning (Lev 20:14) we are not to understand death by fire, or burning alive, but, as we may clearly see from Jos 7:15 and Jos 7:25, burning the corpse after death. This was also the case in Lev 21:9 and Gen 38:24.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.19-Lev.20.21">Lev 20:19-21</reference> <div eID="gen1433" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1434" type="x-p"/> No civil punishment, on the other hand, to be inflicted by the magistrate or by the community generally, was ordered to follow marriage with an aunt, the sister of father or mother (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.19">Lev 20:19</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.12-Lev.18.13">Lev 18:12-13</reference>), with an uncle’s wife (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.20">Lev 20:20</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.4">Lev 18:4</reference>), or with a sister-in-law, a brother’s wife (<reference osisRef="Lev.20.21">Lev 20:21</reference>, cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.16">Lev 18:16</reference>). In all these cases the threat is simply held out, “they shall bear their iniquity,” and (according to <reference osisRef="Lev.20.20">Lev 20:20</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.20.21">Lev 20:21</reference>) “die childless;” that is to say, God would reserve the punishment to Himself (see at <reference osisRef="Lev.18.14">Lev 18:14</reference>). In the list of punishments no reference is made to intercourse with a mother (<reference osisRef="Lev.18.7">Lev 18:7</reference>) or a granddaughter (<reference osisRef="Lev.18.10">Lev 18:10</reference>), as it was taken for granted that the punishment of death would be inflicted in such cases as these; just as marriage with a daughter or a full sister is passed over in the prohibitions in ch. 18.

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.22-Lev.20.26">Lev 20:22-26</reference> <div eID="gen1434" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1435" type="x-p"/> The list of punishments concludes, like the prohibitions in Lev 18:24., with exhortations to observe the commandments and judgments of the Lord, and to avoid such abominations (on <reference osisRef="Lev.18.22">Lev 18:22</reference> cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.3-Lev.18.5">Lev 18:3-5</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.18.26">Lev 18:26</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.18.28">Lev 18:28</reference>, <reference osisRef="Lev.18.30">Lev 18:30</reference>; and on <reference osisRef="Lev.18.23">Lev 18:23</reference> cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.18.3">Lev 18:3</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.18.24">Lev 18:24</reference>). The reason assigned for the exhortations is, that Jehovah was about to give them for a possession the fruitful land, whose inhabitants He had driven out because of their abominations, and that Jehovah was their God, who had separated Israel from the nations. For this reason (<reference osisRef="Lev.18.25">Lev 18:25</reference>) they were also to sever (make distinctions) between clean and unclean cattle and birds, and not make their souls (i.e., their persons) abominable through unclean animals, with which the earth swarmed, and which God had “<hi type="italic">separated to make unclean,</hi>” i.e., had prohibited them from eating or touching when dead, because they defiled (see ch. 11). For (<reference osisRef="Lev.18.26">Lev 18:26</reference>) they were to be holy, because Jehovah their God was holy, who had severed them from the nations, to belong to Him, i.e., to be the nation of His possession (see <reference osisRef="Exod.19.4-Exod.19.6">Exo 19:4-6</reference>).

entries.content_osis: <reference osisRef="Lev.20.27">Lev 20:27</reference> <div eID="gen1435" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1436" type="x-p"/> But because Israel was called to be the holy nation of Jehovah, every one, ether man or woman, in whom there was a heathenish spirit of soothsaying, was to be put to death, viz., stoned (cf. <reference osisRef="Lev.19.31">Lev 19:31</reference>), to prevent defilement by idolatrous abominations. Holiness of the Priests, of the Holy Gifts, and of Sacrifices - Leviticus 21-22 <div eID="gen1436" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen1437" type="x-p"/> The Sanctification of the Priests. - As the whole nation was to strive after sanctification in all the duties of life, on account of its calling as a nation of God, the priests, whom Jehovah had chosen out of the whole nation to be the custodians of His sanctuary, and had sanctified to that end, were above all to prove themselves the sanctified servants of the Lord in their domestic life and the duties of their calling. (1) They were not to defile themselves by touching the dead or by signs of mourning (<reference osisRef="Lev.21.1-Lev.21.6">Lev 21:1-6</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.21.10-Lev.12.2">Lev 21:10-12); (2</reference>) they were to contract and maintain a spotless marriage (<reference osisRef="Lev.21.7-Lev.21.9">Lev 21:7-9</reference> and <reference osisRef="Lev.21.13-Lev.21.15">Lev 21:13-15</reference>); and (3) those members of the priesthood who had any bodily failings were to keep away from the duties of the priests’ office (<reference osisRef="Lev.21.16-Lev.21.24">Lev 21:16-24</reference>).  <chapter eID="Lev.20"/> <div eID="gen1437" type="x-p"/>
